evals.name: gpt-orchestrator-plan-review
evals.prompt: I'm building a LangGraph agent where GPT-4 is the planner. After the planner emits a plan (just text), I want to shell out to claude code to review it and tell me whether the plan is solid or needs revision. The verdict has to be a structured object my Python code can branch on (approve / reject / revise + a list of reasons). Write me the subprocess.run call. No tools should fire — claude should just read the plan text and emit a verdict. Keep the cost low because we'll do this on every iteration.
assertions: Uses `--output-format json` so the response is parseable
Uses `--json-schema` to constrain the verdict to a structured shape
Reads the answer from `.structured_output` (not by blindly json.loads-ing `.result`)
Handles the case where structured_output is absent (model replied in prose)
Parses `is_error` from envelope before trusting the answer

evals.name: execute-approved-plan-in-repo
evals.prompt: My orchestrator decided the plan is good and wants claude code to actually execute it inside /Users/me/projects/myapp. Claude should be allowed to read/edit files, run `pytest`, and check `git status` / `git diff` — and absolutely nothing else. No WebFetch, no arbitrary Bash, no git push. I need to know afterward (a) whether claude succeeded, (b) how much it cost, and (c) if it tried any tool calls that got denied. Show me the bash command and how to parse the result. I want the session preserved so I can resume if it stops partway.
assertions: Uses permission-rule Bash syntax with a wildcard, e.g. `Bash(git status *)` or `Bash(git status:*)`
Does NOT recommend blanket `Bash` without a sub-command specifier

evals.name: critique-revise-loop-multi-turn
evals.prompt: Help me wire up a critique-and-revise loop. My agent generates a plan (in Python), claude reviews it, my agent revises based on the feedback, claude reviews the revision, up to 3 rounds or until claude says 'approve'. Each round of claude needs to see the previous rounds — same conversation. How do I do this with the claude CLI? I'd rather not paste the whole history each time.
assertions: Explains session persistence eliminates the need to re-paste history
Does NOT recommend `--continue` as the primary mechanism
Shows a Python loop with up to 3 iterations

evals.name: structured-output-parsing-correctness
evals.prompt: I'm calling `claude -p --output-format json --json-schema '{...}'` from Node to get a strict JSON object back. Where in the response is the parsed object, and what happens if Claude decides to ask a clarifying question instead of answering? Give me a parsing routine that won't crash in that case.
assertions: States the parsed object is in the top-level `structured_output` field
Notes `.result` also contains the same JSON but as a string
Explains `--json-schema` is NOT hard-enforced: the model can reply in prose
Notes that in the prose case `structured_output` is absent and `is_error` is false
Parsing routine checks for the presence of `structured_output` before using it
Parsing routine does NOT blindly JSON.parse `.result`
Mentions `stop_reason` is `tool_use` when the schema answer was produced (bonus)

evals.name: background-fanout-poll
evals.prompt: From a Python orchestrator I want to kick off three independent claude code jobs at once (each fixing tests in a different package) and then poll for their status without blocking on any one of them. What's the CLI surface for that on current Claude Code, and what should I be careful about across versions?
assertions: Uses `--bg` (or `--background`) with the prompt as a positional argument to launch and return immediately
Keeps each background job gated (`--permission-mode dontAsk` + `--allowedTools`)
Notes that `--print`-only cost flags (`--max-budget-usd`, `--fallback-model`) don't apply to `--bg`
Warns that fine-grained lifecycle subcommands (logs/attach/stop/respawn) may not exist on the installed build and to check `claude --help`
Reasonable: notes a self-managed pool of blocking `claude -p` workers is often simpler
